items.title: Sharing AI progress in mathematics
items.author: OfficialTurkey
items.summary: On August 28, an internal model at OpenAI began training and has since resolved more than 100 long-standing open problems across most areas of mathematics, surprising the mathematicians within the company. This progress has led to discussions on how to inform the mathematical community. Separately, an Advisory Group on Mathematics and AI was announced on September 21, 2026, to advise on the release of these findings but has no power to influence research direction. The mathematical community has expressed concerns, with 25 Fields Medal winners arguing that the focus on solving famous problems as a benchmark by AI companies harms the science of mathematics.

items.title: Mistral Large 4
items.author: Philpax
items.summary: Mistral Large 4 is a 1 trillion-parameter open-weight AI model released by Mistral AI, which aims to leapfrog both American and Chinese rivals. The model can convert technical drawings into CAD models and performs well on semiconductor tests, suggesting it is aimed at industrial customers. Mistral Large 4 reached 67% on the FinWorkBench, level with DeepSeek-V4-Pro and ahead of GLM-5.3, and scored 15% on Harvey’s Legal Agent benchmark. The company plans to use these skills in real-world ways, such as helping insurers assess storm damage in aerial photos, utilities inspect power lines, and farms monitor crop health. Mistral already works with more than 125 large businesses, including Airbus, ASML, and HSBC.

items.title: Strands Decider 2B: a small, open-source, decision model
items.author: gmays
items.summary: Strands Decider 2B is a small, open-source decision model with 2 billion parameters, designed for fast experimentation and local development. It is optimized to return answers to meaningful questions in tens of milliseconds and is suitable for running on a local CPU or GPU. The model is competitive in accuracy and calibration with other models in its class. It is released as open source on GitHub with weights on Hugging Face, including all training data and scripts used to build the model. It is one of a new class of decision models or system one models, designed to pick between sets of options and assign simple numerical scores.

items.title: EmbeddingGemma 2: An open, lightweight multimodal embedding model
items.author: ilreb
items.summary: EmbeddingGemma 2 is an open multimodal embedding model built by Google DeepMind which maps text, images, video, and audio inputs—and combinations thereof—into a single, unified 768-dimensional vector space. The model has 740M total parameters, combining a 270M parameter text model with modular vision (170M) and audio (300M) encoders. It is designed for responsible AI development and is among the strongest multimodal embedding models under 1B parameters, intended for on-device or edge AI applications. The model is lightweight and designed to run on consumer hardware such as mobile devices and laptops, delivering low-latency semantic representations for on-device applications.

items.title: OpenTPU – An open-source AI accelerator, developed by AI
items.author: fsbonetto
items.summary: OpenTPU is an open-source re-implementation of Google's Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) by the UC Santa Barbara ArchLab. It is developed by AI and targets a Xilinx Kintex-7 FPGA on an Inspur PCIe card. The project includes RTL, ISA, a compiler, simulator, and host tools, aiming to test whether AI agents can design the chip that runs their own inference. Reported throughput on LFM2.5-230M is 59.0 tok/s decode and 295.6 tok/s prefill in int8, with DRAM running 82-94% of a 17.1 GB/s peak. The design keeps nothing opaque to make the answer legible: "There is no cache and no hidden scheduling: every data movement is an instruction, so a trace shows exactly where the cycles go."

items.title: ESP32-C3 Adblock
items.author: jayhoon
items.summary: The ESP32-C3 Adblock project, developed by ZedAxis (M-Abozaid on GitHub), is a Pi-hole-class DNS ad-blocker that runs on a $2 ESP32-C3 without requiring PSRAM. It blocks 537,000 ad domains using just 50KB of RAM by storing 5-byte (40-bit) domain hashes in flash and performing binary searches to avoid using RAM. The project can be built from source or flashed via a web interface, and it features a web dashboard for configuration. The sources do not provide specific details on the exact date or version of the firmware used.

items.title: Jev-Driven SRE Diagnosis: What Worked and What Failed
items.author: matt_d
items.summary: According to the sources, Jev is a proprietary AI model developed by TypeSafe AI that was released in limited early access on 15 September 2026. It is a discriminative model used for classification or regression, returning typed values with probability estimates and confidence scores, intended for software consumption rather than human reading. Jev is not fine-tuned with customer data and is trained to return calibrated decisions. It is primarily trained in English, with less accuracy in other languages. Jev is used for high-volume, repeated decisions and is often paired with other models for complex cases that require written explanations. The sources do not provide specific details on what worked and failed with Jev's SRE diagnosis.

items.title: Utah to let AI examine patients and prescribe medication without human oversight
items.author: healsdata
items.summary: Utah has launched a pilot program allowing an AI system to autonomously renew certain prescription medications under state oversight, specifically for patients with chronic conditions. This initiative, conducted through the Utah Department of Commerce and its Office of Artificial Intelligence Policy, focuses on prescription renewals without real-time human clinician involvement. The program raises questions about the future of AI in medical care and the potential for federal legislation to standardize AI-enabled prescribing across states. While the AI system is not authorized to prescribe medications initially, the program represents a significant regulatory development in the use of AI in healthcare.

items.title: Benchmark in Milliseconds
items.author: surprisetalk
items.summary: The sources suggest that for micro benchmarks, a duration of around 300 milliseconds is recommended to keep timings as easy-to-scan integers, avoid skew from fixed costs like interpreter startup, and remain within a human-perceptible range for intuitive judgment. The rule of thumb is to tweak the input size until the benchmark takes about 300ms. For larger benchmarks, the sources mention that anything longer than a second makes iterating on the benchmark slower than it needs to be. In competitive sectors, top-tier properties now consistently serve pages with LCPs under 200 milliseconds.

items.title: South Korea says AI agents appear to have been used to hack the country's banks
items.author: thoughtpeddler
items.summary: South Korean President Lee Jae-myung stated that AI models are believed to have been used in some recent hacking incidents against banks, causing public concern and anxiety. At least seven financial firms, including Shinhan Bank, KB Kookmin Bank, Hana Bank, and Woori Bank, were reportedly hacked, leading to the theft of personal information for 68,000 people. Authorities have not disclosed details on what kind of AI tools were used or the full scale of the breaches. The South Korean police have launched a full-scale investigation into these attacks.

items.title: UniEvo-VL: Self-Distillation Training for Multimodal Model Self-Improvement
items.author: gmays
items.summary: UniEvo-VL is a self-evolving framework for multimodal models to learn from their own constructive self-correction feedback during test-time compute. It leverages the model's self-critiques as privileged information, allowing a single multimodal model to act as both teacher and student with different contexts. The student only sees the vanilla question, while the teacher conditions on the privileged critique. Training minimizes the per-state divergence between their denoising diffusion distributions over the student's own sampling trajectories. Experiments demonstrate that UniEvo-VL improves the image generation capabilities of multimodal models, while maintaining their sensitivity to additional reflection information.

items.title: Integer multiplication below n log n
items.author: E-Reverance
items.summary: The sources indicate that the best-known algorithm for integer multiplication operates in O(n log n) time, as demonstrated by the 2019 algorithm of David Harvey and Joris van der Hoeven. This algorithm uses number-theoretic transforms introduced with the Schönhage–Strassen algorithm. While this is conjectured to be the best possible algorithm, the sources do not provide a definitive answer to whether O(n log n) is a lower bound or if anything beneath n log n would violate it.

items.title: The Early History of Smalltalk (1993)
items.author: _reza
items.summary: The sources indicate that Alan Kay, a computer scientist who won the Turing award, wrote "The Early History of Smalltalk" in 1993. In this paper, Kay discusses the development of Smalltalk and its significance in the context of contemporary programming languages like C++ and the upcoming Java. Kay's narrative emphasizes the idea of simulating virtual computers where each object possesses the Turing completeness of a computer. The paper also mentions that Smalltalk was named to be innocuous, hoping it would pleasantly surprise people if it delivered good results. The Hacker News discussion from 2022 references this paper, highlighting its importance in understanding modern programming languages and computing.

items.title: Erdosproblems.com Succumbs to the AI Onslaught
items.author: pfdietz
items.summary: According to Hacker News, the site erdosproblems.com now primarily serves to advertise AI-generated proofs without explanation, which contrasts with the original vision of the site's founder. Quanta Magazine reports that major tech companies saw an opportunity in the site as a benchmark for AI capabilities. Scientific American notes that AI tools have helped solve about 100 Erdős problems since October, with LLMs often forming new solutions in dialogue with mathematician prompters. The sources collectively indicate a shift in the site's purpose and the impact of AI on solving mathematical problems.

items.title: Nature's capacity to 'bounce back' when species are lost is overestimated: study
items.author: pseudolus
items.summary: The study by King’s College London and Imperial College London with the Natural History found that ecosystems have far less ‘spare’ capacity than previously thought, with the ocean potentially having the most to lose. The idea that ecosystems carry plenty of back-up, so if a small number of species become extinct there is little harm, has been greatly overestimated according to the largest global study of its kind. The study published in Nature Ecology & Evolution combined 423 published studies and 222,829 data points across land, freshwater, marine and estuarine ecosystems. The ecological benefits keep climbing as diversity rises, which means it is falling as we lose species.

I trained this model on undeveloped landscape so that it can quickly add plausible erosion features, rocks, etc to the low-resolution height data and sort of reconstruct what the terrain would look like before any human int

items.title: Chernobyl particles reveal unexpectedly stable nuclear fuel after 40 years
items.author: geox
items.summary: Researchers at Leibniz University Hannover and the Helmholtz-Zentrum Dresden-Rossendorf found that six tiny, highly radioactive fragments released from the destroyed Chernobyl reactor in 1986 have largely intact crystal structures after 40 years, indicating greater chemical stability than previously assumed. The particles retain fission products within themselves, but their structures varied. The findings could allow for more precise assessments of the health risks posed by such radioactive particles. However, samples from only two locations cannot establish regional particle stability or health risks.

items.title: Direct retinal projection display for smart glasses using a meta-optic mirror
items.author: bookofjoe
items.summary: TDK Corporation has demonstrated the world’s first direct retinal projection display for smart glasses using a meta-optic mirror. The mirror is 150 nm thick, uses nanoscale reflectors, and can be embedded directly into a lens. It has a visible-light transmittance of approximately 80 percent, enabling smart glasses with transparency equivalent to that of ordinary eyeglass lenses, making them suitable for everyday use. TDK has also entered into a business cooperation agreement with QD Laser, Inc. to accelerate the development of next-generation RGB light source modules and optical engines for smart glasses.

I've been having a hard time finding a solution. Is there really no commercialized model that I can feed in a reference sound and text instruction and get another sound out?

Right now having a multimodal inputs to image or text output is a commodotized, solved problem. IE you can put a prompt for some image and use a reference image to guide the model on what you want. After all, a picture is worth a thousand words right?

Ive also used a text and audio input in order to get a text descr
items.summary: According to the sources, there is an AI model by Nvidia that can generate sound effects and music from a text description, including novel sounds like making a trumpet bark like a dog. This model, called Fugatto, can also modify existing audio, such as transforming a piano line into a human voice line or changing the accent and mood of a spoken word recording. However, it is not publicly released yet. The sources do not provide information on other commercialized models that can generate sounds based on both text and a reference sound.
